description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of missing pieces and the number of possible solutions for the M-Cube dataset under two different configurations: “Flip needed” and “Flip ignored”. The x-axis, labeled “# Missing pieces”, spans from 1 to 6, with tick marks at each integer value, and is presented on a linear scale without explicit units. The y-axis, labeled “# Possible solutions”, uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² to 10⁸, with tick marks at powers of ten (10², 10⁴, 10⁶, 10⁸). The “Flip needed” configuration is represented by a solid orange line with circle markers, starting at approximately 10² possible solutions when 1 piece is missing and increasing to 10⁸ possible solutions when 6 pieces are missing. The “Flip ignored” configuration is shown as a solid blue line with circle markers, beginning at approximately 10² possible solutions when 1 piece is missing and rising to approximately 10⁶ possible solutions when 6 pieces are missing. Both lines exhibit a consistent upward trend across the x-axis. A red circle highlights the point (6, 10⁸) on the orange line, labeled “CUBE-easy”, and another red circle highlights the point (2, 10²) on the orange line, labeled “CUBE-easy”.
